videos.script: Not every company runs SQL Server. Many run PostgreSQL or MySQL, and pay no licence for either. {{engines}} On Azure, each is a flexible server. One machine, one engine, the major version you pick, and Microsoft doing the patching, the backups and the failover. {{server}} The machine comes in three sizes of family. Burstable for small and quiet, General Purpose for most, and Memory Optimized when the working set is large. {{tiers}} You will run PostgreSQL itself in your container. The same hundred thousand orders, the same customer, the same fifteen rows. {{engine}} Then a setting that needs a restart. On your own server you write it with ALTER SYSTEM. On Azure you are not the superuser, so it goes through the control plane instead. {{params}} Then the three copies a server can have: a standby for the machine, a replica for reading, and a restore for the mistake. {{copies}} And PgBouncer, the pooler built into the server, with MySQL beside it. {{pooler}}
